walkthrough:
**Recall what efficiency means here**

Great start. Efficiency is measured as time taken for dye to reach all parts. So more efficient means faster, which means a shorter time.

Key rule:
$$\text{higher surface area : volume ratio = faster diffusion = higher efficiency}$$

**Use the table to see what controls SA:V**

Volume is fixed at $512 \text{ mm}^3$ for all blocks, so only shape matters. Compare the cube in block 1 with the flat sheet in block 4. Block 1 has SA:V of $0.75$, block 2 (height $2 \text{ mm}$) has $1.3$, and block 4 (height $0.5 \text{ mm}$) has $4.1$. As height falls and the block is flattened, SA:V jumps up.

**Link shape to prediction**

Flattening gives a huge surface for dye to enter and a very short distance to the centre, so time falls and efficiency rises. That matches option C exactly. Increasing height does the opposite, it lowers SA:V, so B cannot be right.

options.A: Width alone does not predict SA:V. For example block 4 has the largest width (32 mm) but also the largest SA:V (4.1), so efficiency would be highest, not lowest.
options.B: As height increases from 0.5 mm in block 4 to 8 mm in block 1, SA:V falls from 4.1 to 0.75, so diffusion gets slower and efficiency decreases, not increases.
options.C: Flattening at fixed volume increases SA:V, from 0.75 in the cube to 4.1 in the flattest block, giving a shorter diffusion distance and faster, more efficient diffusion.
options.D: Elongating at fixed volume tends to increase SA:V, for example length 8 mm gives 0.75 but length 64 mm gives 1.5, so efficiency would increase, not decrease.
